Data Analysis:
Compile, track, and analyze key performance metrics (eCPM, ARPDAU, LTV, Fill Rates) to turn data into actionable revenue strategies.

Experience:
Proven track record managing, growing, and optimizing Video Ads and Offer Wall Campaigns through iOS and Android marketplaces.
Industry Background:
A strong preference for candidates with a background in mobile gaming and a deep passion for the interactive entertainment space.
Analytical Mindset:
Highly skilled at compiling and analyzing complex performance data and metrics to drive decisions.
Soft Skills & Drive:
Self-motivated, driven, and highly comfortable receiving feedback and direction to constantly improve.
Relationship Management:
Strong interpersonal and negotiation skills, with an emphasis on building productive, positive relationships with external partners, management, and peers.
Results-Oriented:
A passion for delivering measurable results and a consistent track record of meeting or exceeding targets.

The Senior Systems Engineer will support technologies spanning endpoint management, patch management, software delivery, vulnerability remediation, endpoint security, configuration management, and automation. Relevant platforms may include Tanium, Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM/MECM), Microsoft Intune, Broadcom Altiris, BigFix, Ivanti, or similar enterprise endpoint management and software distribution technologies. This engineer will partner with architecture, security, infrastructure, and operations teams to continuously improve and mature endpoint services through strategic initiatives, automation, and operational improvements. Senior Systems Engineers are expected to leverage enterprise tooling, scripting, automation, telemetry, and custom applications to monitor service health, optimize performance, troubleshoot complex issues, and improve the reliability and scalability of endpoint services. The role may participate in an on-call rotation supporting routine upgrades, platform maintenance, application support, security remediation, root cause analysis, and post-mortem reviews related to service interruptions or security incidents. The Senior Systems Engineer is expected to operate independently while also serving as a technical mentor to other engineers. jobs.description: We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join a new team delivering Unity platform support for a key platform partner bringing games to TV and mobile form factors. To reach every screen, we will be leveraging both streaming from Linux in the cloud and Web browser builds to be instantly loadable. The team’s goals include delivering stable platform support, realizing developer workflows for Unity users to unlock the unique features of this platform, and leading optimization initiatives to enable Unity to be efficient on the widest possible array of target devices. You have probably worked on performance-critical, cross-platform applications in the past and you know the importance of writing fast, portable and scalable code. You may also be familiar with real-time, browser-based application development using technologies such as HTML5, WebGL/WebGPU, WebAssembly/Emscripten; and/or Linux application technologies such as SDL, Wayland, Linux desktop. What you’ll be doing Working as part of an agile team, to design and develop features and workflows in the Unity Editor to support these specific platform configurations. In collaboration with Unity R&D teams around the world, profile and optimize WebGPU/WebAssembly performance — tackling load times, memory management, and the unique constraints of a browser-hosted Unity runtime. Ensure a stable platform by investigating and resolving bug reports Strengthen quality and delivery through automated testing and thoughtful code reviews — while fostering a culture of innovation, teamwork, and technical excellence. What we’re looking for Strong C++ in a large production codebase. Modern C++, in performance-critical systems where memory, threading, and cache behavior are things you reason about deliberately. Meaningful WebAssembly experience. Emscripten in the browser is the most direct path, but we're open: Rust compiled to Wasm counts, and so does Wasm outside the browser — server-side compute, Node, edge runtimes, or work on the runtimes and toolchain themselves. If you've wrestled with binary size, startup time, linear memory, or the host interop boundary, that's what we're after. Solid understanding of how applications span languages and runtimes. How synchronous and asynchronous calls cross the boundary, and how memory is owned and marshalled between them. Proficiency with profiling tools across CPU, GPU, I/O, and memory — and the habit of measuring before optimizing. Experience designing and implementing scalable features in a large multithreaded codebase. Working proficiency in C#. Unity's Editor and much of its tooling is C#, and you'll write it. Deep prior C# isn't required if your systems fundamentals are strong. You might also have (optional) Familiarity with real time 3D rendering techniques and graphics APIs including WebGPU and/or Vulkan A methodical approach to researching and developing innovative optimization solutions A passion for the future of computer games or real-time 3D experiences in a variety of settings Familiarity with how to best use AI in the software development process. jobs.description: As a System Development Engineer , you will take ownership of key workstreams within Amazon's Region Flexibility Migration team, driving critical infrastructure migration initiatives that enable Amazon's services to operate across multiple AWS regions. You will lead the development of automation frameworks, mentor junior engineers, and make technical decisions that shape the Boost Accelerator program's roadmap. you will drive efforts aimed at optimizing memory utilization across service fleets, identifying opportunities to right-size allocations, reduce infrastructure footprints, and preserve capacity to support continued growth and expansion. Join a team where you will have a direct impact on reducing migration burden for service teams and delivering zero-impact migrations at massive scale. Key job responsibilities ● Design, implement, maintain, and deploy components that solve problems in a complex ecosystem. We work in lots of different languages (not limited to, but most often Python and Java). It is more important to us that you understand coding in the context of working in distributed systems and/or widely scaled web applications. ● Lead migration projects from planning through execution, including infrastructure setup, data replication, traffic management, and post-migration validation ● Identify and implement cost optimization strategies to reduce per-offering costs of the Boost program through automation and streamlined operations. ● Drive technical decisions for Boost program offerings, including pipeline infrastructure setups, DDB replication, containerization solutions, and new offerings such as RDS, DocumentDB, and VFI builds. ● Mentor and guide junior engineers, conducting code reviews, providing technical direction, and fostering a culture of operational excellence within the team. ● Lead root cause analysis for high-severity incidents, implement preventive measures, and drive operational improvements across the team's processes and tooling. ● Collaborate with service teams across Amazon to identify and resolve migration blockers ● Participate in on-call rotations to ensure operational support for critical migration activities ● Building AI-assisted workflows that streamline migration operation or make our day to day job easier and faster. ● Perform deep dive on services with different compute type to generate recommendations for optimization of resources. A day in the life You will lead the technical direction for complex migration challenges using AWS technologies and modern development practices. You might collaborate with our Boost program team on pipeline infrastructure setups, build AI-assisted workflows that streamline migration operations, or develop tools in Python and Java to automate critical migration tasks. You'll work closely with service teams across Amazon to identify and resolve migration obstacles, analyze memory efficiency across service fleets, and contribute to expanding our Boost program offerings. Your work will span infrastructure setup, data replication, traffic management, and post-migration validation, all while supporting operational excellence through monitoring, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement. You'll also mentor team members, participate in design reviews, and collaborate with Seattle-based leadership on strategic priorities. About the team The Region Flexibility Migration (RFM) team is part of Amazon's Intelligent Cloud Hosting (ICON) organization. The RFM team was formed in 2024 with the purpose of proactively discovering and mitigating issues that service teams would encounter when migrating services across AWS regions like eu-south-2 and eu-central-1. During the last year and a half, the team has developed expertise in identifying these issues and leveraging those findings to save builder effort. The team has also developed expertise in identifying undifferentiated work within these migration workloads and created the Boost program that reduces the migration burden for service teams by offloading foundational and undifferentiated migration work to a central team.
